- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was neutral or positive; apply dampening factor to subsequent days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in early days (first 5-7 days), especially if sentiment is volatile; add 1-2% downward bias for first 7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply corrective shift 3-5 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending downward; increase forecast by 1-3% to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Avoid over-reliance on recent high sentiment peaks; if sentiment peaks > 1.00 for 3+ consecutive days, apply 5-10% downward correction to avoid over-optimism.
